close_reason: Took option (a): removed literal '(10)' from DepthExceeded variant doc and Display string; both now reference 'configured maximum'/PathBuilderConfig::max_depth/DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH. Variant remains a unit (no breaking change).
description:
## Anchor
Pass-2 commit e586bc49 closed PKIX-qwzx.8 ("pkix-path-builder doc 'tries 1..10' is stale for build_path_with_config"). The Algorithm rustdoc was updated correctly (pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:18-26 now references PathBuilderConfig::max_depth and DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH).

## Finding
Two doc-vs-code sites still hardcode '(10)':

pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:133
```rust
/// the maximum depth (10) this builder supports.
DepthExceeded,
```

pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:155 (Display impl)
```rust
Self::DepthExceeded => f.write_str(
    "maximum intermediate chain depth (10) exceeded; the chain may require a deeper path than this builder supports",
),
```

When a caller supplies `PathBuilderConfig { max_depth: 5, ... }`, the resulting Display string still says "depth (10) exceeded". This is misleading.

## Severity
P3. Pure docs; no behavior wrong. But it's the same user-visible drift PKIX-qwzx.8 was filed to fix — closure was incomplete.

## Fix
Either (a) drop the literal "(10)" from both sites and reference PathBuilderConfig::max_depth, OR (b) thread the actual max_depth into the error variant (`DepthExceeded { max_depth: usize }`) — the latter is a minor breaking change.

Option (a) is the lower-risk close: the variant doc and Display string both can say "the configured maximum (default DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 10)".

## Pass-2 attribution
PKIX-qwzx.8 closure: partial.
title: P3: pkix-path-builder DepthExceeded Display/doc still hardcodes '(10)' after PathBuilderConfig::max_depth was made configurable
